style.track: prototype: no framework implements this strategy
style.components: no components: the sheet is one static HTML string parsed once, every element is E[n] (its place in document order, labels and options left out); the items are a row template cloned per row
style.messages: erased for DOM events: each update arm is inlined into the action its control calls (an input's setter P.name, an item's handler in its row)
style.derivedValues: static edges and memoization, with a runtime rank-ordered flush: every formula is a node that recomputes its value once per flush, in dependency order (a sorted queue of nodes ranked, when the module runs, by creation order), with an equality cut-off (a list or a group compares its items); the readers of a cell are written into the cell's own code, static (written at build time), so nobody registers at mount
style.cutoff: yes: a formula whose value did not change queues no reader and paints nothing; a top-k list always repaints its keyed list (a field of a listed item may have changed in place) but cuts off its readers
style.displays: a display that reads one cell is inlined into that cell's code; one that reads several is a function that each of its cells collects and that runs after the formulas
style.itemEdits: an item edit writes the item in place and queues the formulas that read the field it wrote (by qty, by active) or, for a change to the set of items, every formula that reads the items; no incremental aggregates: each affected formula recomputes over the items
style.lists: keyed by id: rows.js for the items table (reconcile on a replaced array, add/drop in place), runtime.js list for the top-k lists
style.externalEvents: receive(msg): serverInputs through the input actions, serverItems and snapshot move copies of the message's data into the state; a snapshot is applied like the initial state
style.build: Vite with no framework plugin, production defaults, hidden source maps

style.state: <let> per input, and for the markup, the items, nextId and rng

style.externalEvents: app.marko <return>s a function that assigns the <let>s; serverInputs and snapshot go through one setInput switch; dispatched items are copied, never adopted

style.components: one instance per input (model: its value), per formula (model: its last value, the cache the compiler keeps) and one for the items section; no chunking by position or count. A unit's displays are the binding list of its formula's instance, an input's control the binding list of the input's instance
style.reads: a formula is a reader: it watches the cells its expression reads and is sent its one message when one changes; its binding list also watches the cells its displays read. A value that did not change (=== , or the same items for a list) tells nobody. Jobs run in rank order, so a formula is recomputed once after the cells it reads
style.formulas: each expression compiled into its formula's arm; generic collection helpers (sum, avg, top, groupSum) take the formula's own function; lists and group sums are cached as arrays and compared item by item
style.items: quiet=analysed (default): an arm that writes only fields outside R, the item fields read by a formula or display, does not notify the readers (a compile-time rule applied to every arm, tea-inline's analysis at one bit per arm); quiet=none: every arm notifies
style.events: controls wired by position (wire) to the cell that owns them; the rows by one delegated listener per event type on the table body
style.externalEvents: serverInputs sets the named inputs, serverItems is a message of the items instance, a snapshot sets every input and the items instance
style.lists: runtime keyed list for the top-k lists (src/runtime.js) and the minimal-move keyed table for the items (src/table.js)
style.dom: each unit's markup as one static template (trailing end tags left out), placeholders for dynamic texts
style.build: Vite production build, no framework plugin, hidden source maps

style.model: hand-written style: plain let variables for the inputs and formulas, a state object for the items, records edited in place
style.formulas: one calcX() per formula, its own expression as JavaScript, returning whether the value changed (=== for numbers, bools and texts; lists and group sums always count as changed)
style.derived: waves: a change recomputes what it feeds, in dependency order, as straight-line code per trigger (changeX per input; itemsChanged, qtyChanged, activeChanged for the items); a formula downstream runs only if a formula it reads changed (the floor in work)
style.displays: one showX() per cell writing the text nodes that read it (textContent); a node reading several cells is a function every one of them calls; found by position in a static markup string
style.lists: top-k lists through a generic keyed-list helper (src/lib.js, runtime) that keeps the <li> of an item that stays; group rows are static <li>s
style.items: rows cloned from a <tr> template, records carrying their <tr>; server items and snapshots through the generic keyed reconciler (src/lib.js, runtime), fed copies of the message's items
style.events: delegated click, input and change listeners per section, switching on data-role; a number input sends only while valid; controls written only when they differ
style.helpers: src/util.js (app code): PRNG step, formatters, sumBy/avgBy/maxBy/minBy/topBy/groupSum taking the formula's own code as a function
style.build: Vite with no framework plugin, production defaults, hidden source maps

style.architecture: TEA with Browser.element: one Model (a record field per input, items, markup, nextId, rng), one Msg (a constructor per control and per item control), one update (a case branch per message as record updates), one view
style.derived: naive TEA: computed in view. viewSheet opens with a let binding every formula, in dependency order, to its own expression over model and the formulas above it, so each is computed once per view; the model caches nothing, update stays one-field record updates; every event recomputes every formula (Html.Lazy skips rows, not formulas)
style.rows: Html.Keyed.node "tbody" with ( String.fromInt item.id, lazy2 viewRow model.markup item ); items replaced, never mutated, by mapItem id (a missing id is a no-op)
style.lists: top-k lists and group sums as Html.Keyed lists (by item id, by category)
style.numbers: Int throughout; division is floor (toFloat a / toFloat b) (fdiv), never // (32-bit); number input messages come from onNumber, an input decoder that fails (no message, no redraw) unless the text is an integer in range
style.externalEvents: one incoming port events : (Value -> msg) -> Sub msg, decoded with Json.Decode into ServerInputs (Dict String Value, read per input by readInputs), ServerItems and Snapshot
style.helpers: src/Util.elm (app code): Item, PRNG step and word pools, formatters, sumBy/avgBy/maxBy/minBy/topBy/groupSum, decoders, attribute helpers
style.formatting: as elm-format 0.8.8 writes it (an if is a whole binding body, or bound to a name of its own); elm.json lists only the dependencies the app imports
style.build: elm make --optimize, then uglify-js compress (pure_funcs) and mangle passes, as the Elm guide recommends

style.components: the sheet is one module (cells as module-level lets and cell functions, arms, DOM built once from one static template); the items section is another; every formula, display and control is written out as code from the spec, nothing interpreted at runtime
style.state: one immutable TEA model in the reference's shape; formulas are not state: each stores its value in a module-level variable, computed once per change
style.dirtyBits: one bit per cell (a formula, a display or a control), numbered so each cell comes after the cells it reads; an arm marks the bits of the cells that read the field it wrote (IN[name]); a flush sweeps the marked cells in ascending order
style.derivedValues: a formula recomputes when marked, compares with its stored value and marks its readers only when it changed (numbers, booleans and words by !==, a filtered list by the identity of its items; a top-k list and a group sum count as changed every time they are recomputed)
style.items: item edits mark the formulas that read the edited field (a quantity, the active flag) with compile-time bits, structural changes mark every formula that reads the items, a note marks none; formulas over the items recompute in full (no incremental aggregates)
style.rows: one cloned template per row, patched by column bits (quantity, active, note, markup), as in big-table; events delegated by data-role
style.externalEvents: through the same send: serverInputs sets the named inputs through the same arms, serverItems reconciles the table and marks the formulas over the items, snapshot marks every cell and reconciles the table
style.build: Vite with no framework plugin, production defaults, hidden source maps

style.components: Sheet (every formula, then the units' displays), Items (toolbar and table), ItemRow, NumberInput; props, no context; no formula descriptors, nothing interpreted
style.state: one useReducer in App over { inputs, markup, items, nextId, rng }; immutable updates with structural sharing; load and addItem draw from the app's generator inside the reducer
style.derived: computed during render in Sheet, one const per formula in dependency order; no useMemo (the compiler variant memoizes the same source)
style.lists: .map with key: rows and top-k items by id, group rows by category
style.displays: JSX text children reading the formulas' consts; formatters from src/util.js
style.inputs: controlled, onChange; NumberInput reports only integers in range and keeps a draft of other text until the record it reads changes
style.externalEvents: a subscription in a useEffect dispatching each message to the reducer
style.helpers: src/util.js (app code): PRNG step, formatters, sumBy/avgBy/maxBy/minBy/topBy/groupSum taking the formula's own code as a function
style.build: Vite + @vitejs/plugin-react, production defaults, hidden source maps

attribution: source maps: node_modules → runtime; unmapped bundler output → tooling (counted with runtime); the adapter file → adapter (excluded); everything else → app. Brotli split: runtime = brotli(runtime+tooling); app = brotli(app JS) − runtime.
